text: DUNMARROW, Sept. 18 — The planned Dunmarrow canal tunnel will run 11 kilometres, people familiar with the matter said on Wednesday, confirming a core figure in the inland waterway project’s revised design. The Boreal Transit Authority is expected to submit the updated route package next week, after engineers trimmed two access shafts and shifted the eastern portal 600 metres north to avoid unstable clay. Project managers now estimate the tunnel will cost 4.8 billion merks, up from an earlier 4.1 billion estimate, and could open in late 2031 if permitting stays on schedule. The canal link is intended to move grain and fertilizer around the Blackmere bend, easing congestion at the old river locks.
